title: A Veil for the Garden
premise: Sable Brightwater, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has hidden her magic for twelve years in the city of Corvane, where magic is outlawed and her order was slaughtered. When a century-old prophecy book surfaces naming tonight's date as the night the veil between realms collapses, Sable is dragged into a war between the mortal city and the garden realm of Virelai, whose dying covenant once fed both worlds. To reforge it, she must gather three shattered oath-stones, confront the magistrate who ordered her order's destruction, and accept that survival bought by silence was never truly living. In the end, Sable speaks the broken oath aloud at terrible personal cost, sealing herself as the living bridge between realms — not as a sacrifice, but as a woman who finally belongs to both worlds at once.
about_author: Sable Ashgrove is the pen name of a former botanist who spent a decade cataloguing endangered plants before turning to fiction, and it shows in every garden she writes. She lives near the coast with an ill-tempered cat and a greenhouse full of things that bloom out of season.

chapters.title: Charms for Copper
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Twelve years after the Purge, Sable sells harmless charms in Corvane's night market, hiding her swordspeaker gift behind small trades and smaller lies. A nervous customer pays with an old coin stamped with her order's sigil. The emotional beat is the ache of a life shrunk down to fit inside fear.

chapters.title: The Book That Knew Tonight
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The coin's seller, an archivist named Wren Halloway, shows her a prophecy book written a century ago — and tonight's date is inked on its final page beside Sable's true name. She refuses to believe it until the words begin rewriting themselves as she watches. The beat: dread arriving like cold water.

chapters.title: What the Magistrate Burns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Magistrate Corvel Dain raids the archive hunting prophecy texts, revealing he knows the veil is failing and intends to let it fall rather than honor any covenant with Virelai. Wren escapes with the book but is marked. The beat: the machinery of state fear grinding into motion.

chapters.title: The Garden Bleeds Through
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At midnight, the veil tears above the market square; Virelai's overgrown beauty spills into the city, gorgeous and lethal. Sable's suppressed gift ignites involuntarily, saving strangers and exposing her. The beat: terror and exhilaration tangled together — her power feels like coming home.

chapters.title: Arrested by the Man Who Signed the Order
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Dain arrests Sable personally, and she recognizes him: he led the Purge as a young officer. In his cells she learns he keeps a dying Virelai sapling caged, feeding it just enough to keep himself alive. The beat: hatred complicated by recognition — they are both survivors of the same night.

chapters.title: The Fox Who Owes a Debt
chapters.summary: Tam Vess, a shapeshifting exile from Virelai, breaks Sable out, claiming her grandmother saved his life and the debt transfers to her. He carries the first oath-stone shard embedded in his shoulder like a splinter he cannot remove. The beat: reluctant alliance, banter masking grief.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, flashback-woven. Fleeing through the undercity, Sable finally tells Tam what happened during the Purge — how she survived by swearing silence while her mentor died speaking the oath. Tam reveals the oath can only be reforged by a speaker who admits why she stopped. The beat: confession as the first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: The Orchard of Names
chapters.summary: Sable and Tam cross into Virelai's borderlands, where trees grow around the names of the dead oath-bound, including her mentor's. The second stone rests there, guarded by a warden who tests Sable with illusions of the life she could have had. The beat: temptation, and choosing truth over comfort.

chapters.title: The Warden's Price
chapters.summary: Warden Ilex's POV. The warden agrees to yield the stone only if Sable takes up her mentor's unfinished vow — binding herself to return and tend the orchard. Sable accepts without fully understanding the cost. The beat: inheritance accepted too quickly, foreshadowing the ending's weight.

chapters.title: Dain's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. The magistrate offers Wren freedom in exchange for tracking Sable, revealing his own history: he watched the old covenant fail his family and believes all magic is a debt collectors' scheme. The beat: making the antagonist legible without forgiving him.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Returning to Corvane, Sable finds neighborhoods quietly starving as Virelai's withheld seasons bite — the covenant's break hurts mortals too. She begins healing small wounds publicly, and people start remembering what magic gave them. The beat: belonging rebuilt one stranger at a time.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Wren, tracked by Dain's men, leads them unknowingly to Sable. The third stone, hidden in the bell tower where her order once trained, is seized mid-retrieval; Tam is gravely wounded shielding her. The beat: guilt, fury, and the shattering of the plan.

chapters.title: What Grief Costs
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hiding in the undercity, Sable tends Tam and nearly uses forbidden blood-magic to save him — the same shortcut that corrupted the original covenant. Wren arrives, confessing her betrayal, and begs to help. The beat: mercy chosen over vengeance, barely.

chapters.title: The Root Beneath the Prison
chapters.summary: Sable and Wren infiltrate Dain's keep and discover the caged sapling is the covenant's last living root — Dain has been unknowingly keeping the door open. The stones must be joined to the root, in the heart of enemy ground. The beat: the map of the climax drawn in enemy territory.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Greenhouse Cell
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confronts Dain before the sapling, and instead of dueling, makes him speak his grief aloud — his wife died because the failing covenant couldn't heal her. For one moment they are two mourners. Then he still refuses, and calls his guards. The beat: empathy that fails, and hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Veil
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Dain, desperate, attempts to destroy the root and sever Virelai forever; the veil begins collapsing city-wide, gardens and streets bleeding together catastrophically. Tam, half-healed, holds the breach open with his own body. The beat: everything breaking at once.

chapters.title: Three Stones, One Voice
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Amid the collapse, Sable joins the three shards at the root and begins the oath — but the words stall at the line she swore silence over twelve years ago. Her mentor's voice, or memory of it, asks her the question she fled. The beat: the story's whole theme compressed into one held breath.

chapters.title: Why I Stopped Speaking
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confesses it fully: she survived because she ran, and she has punished herself ever since. Speaking the truth completes the oath — the covenant accepts not a perfect knight but an honest survivor. The beat: catharsis; the price of survival finally paid in truth instead of silence.

chapters.title: The Bridge Made Flesh
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The reforged covenant demands a living anchor, and Sable accepts the warden's vow made real: she becomes the bridge, rooted in both worlds, no longer fully mortal nor fully spirit. Dain, witnessing, lowers his weapon. The beat: transformation as fulfillment, not loss.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Winter
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Stripped of office, Dain tends the freed sapling in the public garden built on the ruins of his keep — penance as gardening. Wren brings him the prophecy book, its final page now blank. The beat: an antagonist given an ending earned rather than imposed.

chapters.title: Two Worlds, One Market
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A year later, Corvane's night market sells charms openly beside Virelai's fruit; Tam runs messages between realms; Wren archives a new book that writes itself forward, hopefully. Sable visits her mentor's tree in the orchard of names. The beat: belonging achieved, quiet and specific.

chapters.title: A Veil, Not a Wall
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, closing chapter. Standing at the threshold between realms on the anniversary of the Purge, Sable reflects that veils exist so both sides choose to meet — and she is the meeting place now. She steps through, home on either side. The beat: peace, and the promise that the story's world goes on breathing.
